answer_1.quote: The methodology section is most relevant in identifying plagiarism. Any other sections apart from these 4 are usually irrelevant.
answer_1.outputs: research proposals containing a title, problem statement, motivation, proposed method, experiment plan, test cases, and a fall back plan

answer_2.quote: To systematically evaluate automated plagiarism detection methods, we create a synthetic dataset of research proposals intentionally plagiarized from existing papers.

answer_3.quote: Claude 3.5 Sonnet performs pairwise comparisons between the proposal and each of these top 10 papers. The LLM determines if the proposal and the retrieved paper are substantially similar, discarding the proposal if they are.

answer_4.quote: Twelve participants each evaluate 3 out of 5 proposals that align with their domain knowledge, resulting in 3 × 12 = 36 total proposals.
answer_4.guideline: Participants are asked to only consider papers available until April 2024... Using a consistent evaluation rubric (see Table 1), participants assign similarity scores from 1-5 to each proposal.
